terms.meaning: "Sacred writings": the Egyptian script of small drawings.
A dead body preserved with chemicals and wrapped in thin cloth.
The title of Egypt's kings. It means a person who lives in a palatial house.
The writing system the Sumerians developed in Mesopotamia.

"The First Citizen of the State": the title Octavius took.

items.name: Why the Nile mattered
items.formula: Its yearly flood left a layer of fertile clay soil on the valley.
items.example: Egypt also gave us the calendar and complex irrigation.

items.name: Egyptian belief about death
items.formula: Each person answers to Osiris, god of life after death, for their deeds.
items.example: So tall stone towers, called Pyramids by the Greeks, were built over graves.

items.name: The Hyksos in Egypt
items.formula: An Arabian shepherd tribe that ruled for 500 years.
items.example: Thebes rose against them in 1700 B.C.E. and drove them out.

items.name: Cleopatra
items.formula: The last Egyptian queen, defeated by Augustus in 30 B.C.E.
items.example: Egypt then became a province of Rome.

items.name: Meaning of Mesopotamia
items.formula: "Land between the rivers": the Euphrates and Tigris.
items.example: The name was given by the Greeks.

items.name: The Hanging Gardens
items.formula: A wonder of the Old World, on the Euphrates, around the 7th century B.C.E.
items.example: Most credit Nebuchadnezzar II, who built them for his wife Amitis.

items.name: Code of Hammurabi
items.formula: Hammurabi, the famous Amorite king, enforced "an eye for an eye".
items.example: Edicts found in 1901 are now in the Louvre in Paris.

items.name: Peoples who ruled Mesopotamia, in order
items.formula: Sumerians, Akkadians, Amorites, Hittites, Assyrians, Chaldeans.
items.example: Sumerians arrived in 4000 B.C.E.; Persians attacked in the 6th century B.C.E.

items.name: China's Sorrow
items.formula: The Hwang Ho river.
items.example: Its floods changed course without warning and ruined homes, fields and canals.

items.name: First Chinese dynasties
items.formula: Shang: 18th to 12th century B.C.E. Then the Chau ruled until 250 B.C.E.
items.example: Chau kings gave land to officials in return for support in war.

items.name: The Great Wall of China
items.formula: Qin Shihuangti ordered the northern walls joined. Work ran from the 7th century B.C.E. to the 16th century C.E.
items.example: It stretches more than 5000 km.

items.name: Chinese gifts to the world
items.formula: Porcelain and the Great Wall; also silk.
items.example: Glazed porcelain had developed by the Han dynasty (200 B.C.E.).

items.name: Greek life
items.formula: They called themselves Hellenese, believed gods lived on Mount Olympus, and held Olympic Games every 4 years.
items.example: There were no priests; the king prayed for all.

items.name: Alexander
items.formula: King of Macedonia and pupil of Aristotle. He defeated Persia and marched to India.
items.example: He died at Babylonia in 323 B.C.E.

items.name: Patricians and Plebeians
items.formula: Patricians: rich landowners who controlled the Senate. Plebeians: common people with few rights.
items.example: After their 5th century B.C.E. revolt, Plebeians could choose the Tribunes.

items.name: Punic Wars
items.formula: Rome against Carthage for control of Sicily, for 118 years.
items.example: Carthage lost.

items.name: Spartacus
items.formula: He led about 60,000 slaves in revolt against Rome.
items.example: It was crushed after one year.

items.name: End of the Roman Republic
items.formula: Brutus killed Julius Caesar. Caesar's nephew Octavius then ruled as Augustus for 44 years.
items.example: Later rulers were dictators and Rome declined.

items.name: The Mayas
items.formula: Yucatan in Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras; language Yucutec.
items.example: The earliest cities date from about 320 C.E.

items.name: The Aztecs
items.formula: Their city Tenochtitlan stood on an island in Lake Texcoco; language Nahua.
items.example: The Spanish entered the Mexican valley in 1519 C.E. and conquered them.

items.name: The Incas
items.formula: 15th and 16th centuries, across Peru, Ecuador, Chile and Argentina.
items.example: They were skilled in gold work, and the Sun God was their main deity.

mistakes.text: Egypt: hieroglyphics. Mesopotamia: cuneiform. Harappa's script is a third one, still unread.
The Hanging Gardens did not hang in the air. Plants grew on terraces and their branches hung down.
The Hwang Ho gave China its start but is called its sorrow, because of its floods.
